chapter_theme: A song at Perumpuliyur (பெரும்புலியூர்): the poet, sunk in women's beds, asks Murugan to pity him and give his two feet; the praise names him son of Chidambaram and of Sivakami.

891.reading: The poet describes women with anklets and jingling ornaments, breasts heaving, earrings swinging, peacock-like and laughing, and asks Murugan, who sees him sunk with them on the bed, to pity him a little and give his two feet. The praise names Murugan the son of Chidambaram on the peacock with his kadamba garland, the one at whose anger the asuras were uprooted and vultures fed on heaped corpses, the son of Sivakami, the radiant Abhirami, who went to the millet field and joined the kura girl, at Perumpuliyur.
891.nuance: சிதம்பரகுமார and சிவகாமி: the praise names Murugan through Chidambaram's dancer and his consort, near Perumpuliyur (புலியூர் is also Chidambaram's old name). பெதும்பை எழு கோலம் may refer to the seven stages of a woman's life.
